newsitem.title: USA: UK's Blair wants Labour to be party of business.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair wants Labour to be party of business.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair met leading U.S. financiers and industrialists on Monday as part of a continuing charm offensive aimed at making his ruling Labour party a natural ally of business.

Among the movers and shakers invited to a round table discussion with Blair were the heads of investment banks Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers and the vice-chairmen of J.P. Morgan, Citibank and Bankers Trust.

Also due to attend was Stanley Druckenmiller, the managing director of Soros Fund Management, whose founder George Soros made a killing at Britain's expense when he correctly speculated that sterling would be forced out of Europe's exchange rate mechanism in September 1992.
Blair has made a determined effort to woo business both before and since his landslide election victory on May 1, when Labour ended 18 years of Conservative rule in Britain.

"I want the Labour party to be the party of business -- the party that says we need a thriving, competitive business sector and that we need to be able to operate effectively in international markets," Blair told reporters before the meeting.
It was his last engagement after a four-day U.S. trip to the annual summit of the Group of Seven industrial nations in Denver and to an environmental summit at the the United Nations.

Aides said Blair would argue that Labour was now better placed than the Conservatives -- the traditional voice of business in Britain -- to represent British industry and finance because of its more positive stance on Europe.

He said he would explain his plans to improve education and reform Britain's welfare state to ensure everyone is equipped to find work in a rapidly changing economy -- a strategy that steers a course between outdated state interventionism and unbridled free markets.
"That is a different, a third, way forward from the politics of the past and I think it gains a lot of support not just in the country but amongs the business community as well," Blair said.
